page: Microsoft Azure F1amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance configured with 1 dedicated vCPU and 1 physical core powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD. The processor includes an L3 cache of 32 MB, an L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and an L1d cache of 48 KB. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), cryptography standards (AES, VAES, SHA_NI), and virtualization extensions (SVM).

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance of the AMD EPYC processor is highly competitive. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance is limited to a single dedicated vCPU, its multi-core performance in stress-ng and overall PassMark CPU metrics are positioned in the lower tier. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is relatively low, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tier performance. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are also limited by the single-core constraint, placing them in the lower performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1amds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated high-frequency CPU resources without the overhead of multi-core licensing or allocation costs. The inclusion of a 118 GB local NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space. This configuration is best suited for single-threaded workloads that require a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose instances, such as light memory-intensive analytical tasks, single-threaded data processing, small-scale caching, or low-concurrency utility services.
